fu.t: During Hu Jintao's return visit to Brasília, Brazil recognises China's market-economy status. The agreements signed include a poultry protocol, an ethanol memorandum, satellite agreements and an extradition treaty.
The 2011 China–Brazil joint communiqué says Brazil 'reaffirmed its commitment' to recognise China's market-economy status. The recognition therefore remained an open commitment seven years later.

timeline.ev: During Hu Jintao's November 2004 visit to Buenos Aires, Argentina and China sign five framework agreements (space, tourism, railways, education, economic complementation). Private Chinese firms sign letters of intent for projected investments of US$19.71bn over ten years, including US$8bn for railways, US$5bn for hydrocarbons and US$6bn for housing.
timeline.sg: State visit within Hu's 2004 Latin America tour
timeline.src: Página/12: Página/12, El País section, 17 November 2004

fu.t: iProfesional (2022) reports that the announced money never reached Argentina. It adds that in March 2005 a Chinese embassy official said Hu's delegation did not recognise the investments announced by the Argentine government.

timeline.ev: George W. Bush meets Álvaro Uribe in Cartagena after APEC Santiago. Bush says the US has provided more than US$3bn under Plan Colombia since 2000, will ask Congress to renew support, and is working on a free trade agreement linking the US, Colombia and other Andean nations.
timeline.sg: Security cooperation (Plan Colombia) and trade
timeline.src: The White House (George W. Bush archives): Press Availability with President Bush and President Uribe of Colombia
timeline.loc: Escuela Naval de Cadetes Almirante Padilla, Cartagena

fu.t: The US and Colombia sign the Trade Promotion Agreement (existing record X-E207; it enters into force in 2012, X-E030). The source is in those records.

timeline.ev: On Hu Jintao's state visit to Mexico (September 2005), Hu and Vicente Fox sign seven trade agreements, including access for Mexican grapes and pears. Fox says bilateral trade of nearly US$15bn a year strongly favours China, and Mexican business groups complain about smuggled Chinese goods.
timeline.sg: State visit; trade and UN reform
timeline.src: China Daily: Hu, Fox sign trade agreements (China Daily, 13 September 2005)

timeline.ev: Evo Morales declares US Ambassador Philip Goldberg persona non grata, accusing him of conspiring with the opposition. The US expels Bolivian Ambassador Gustavo Guzmán the next day, and Hugo Chávez expels US Ambassador Patrick Duddy in solidarity.
timeline.sg: Documented diplomatic tension (expulsion of ambassadors)
timeline.src: CBS News / Associated Press: Diplomats Ousted As U.S.-Latin Row Deepens

fu.t: Bolivia's interim government names Walter Serrate ambassador to the US, the first after 11 years in which both countries were represented only by chargés d'affaires. Senate approval was still pending.
At Rodrigo Paz's inauguration, both governments pledge to restore full diplomatic relations (existing record X-E275; the source is in that record).

timeline.ev: Barack Obama visits Mexico City and, with Felipe Calderón, announces a US–Mexico Bilateral Framework on Clean Energy and Climate Change. It covers renewables, efficiency, adaptation, carbon-market tools, cross-border grids and border-region wind and solar, and the US backs Mexico hosting COP16.
timeline.sg: First presidential visit; energy, climate, security
timeline.src: The White House (Obama archives): U.S.-Mexico Announce Bilateral Framework on Clean Energy and Climate Change

timeline.ev: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner meets Hu Jintao in Beijing in the middle of China's soybean-oil import freeze. Argentina signs rail contracts that AFP reports at US$10bn across ten projects; the Belgrano Cargas refurbishment accounts for US$10bn by AS/COA's account. A CDB–Banco Nación US$150m credit line is also signed.
timeline.sg: State visit; investment, rail, trade dispute (soybean oil)
timeline.src: AFP (via SpaceDaily/SolarDaily): China, Argentina agree 10 billion dollars in rail deals
timeline.loc: Great Hall of the People, Beijing

fu.t: Timerman says the soybean-oil dispute was not resolved during the trip and was not its main objective.
The Buenos Aires Grain Exchange says China stopped buying Argentine soy oil in April and the conflict still needs resolving; exports diverted to India at about US$50/t less.

timeline.ev: On Dilma Rousseff's state visit, Hu Jintao and Rousseff sign a joint communiqué. China pledges to encourage imports of higher-value Brazilian goods, Brazil reaffirms its commitment to recognise China's market-economy status, and the communiqué covers aviation cooperation with Embraer, high-speed rail, the first pork export approvals and CBERS satellites. Around the visit, a US$12bn Foxconn plan for Brazil was announced.
timeline.sg: State visit (12–13 April 2011)
timeline.src: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC: Joint Communiqué of the PRC and the Federative Republic of Brazil (full text)

fu.t: Tecnoblog reports there was 'nenhum sinal' of the US$12bn promised for the technology sector. Foxconn's Itu plant (announced 2012, R$1bn initial) remained empty, against 100,000 jobs promised.

timeline.ev: Rousseff visits the White House. The joint statement launches a US–Brazil Strategic Energy Dialogue and an aviation partnership MoU, backs Science Without Borders and 100,000 Strong in the Americas, and commits to faster US visa processing and new consulates in Belo Horizonte and Porto Alegre.
timeline.sg: Official working visit
timeline.src: The White House (Obama archives): Joint Statement by President Obama and President Rousseff

fu.t: The full state visit planned for October 2013 is postponed over NSA surveillance (record X-E1010).

timeline.ev: Rousseff postpones her October 2013 state visit to Washington after revelations that the NSA intercepted her communications and those of Petrobras. Her office calls it a serious act violating national sovereignty, and the White House says the visit 'should not be overshadowed by a single bilateral issue'.
timeline.sg: Documented tension: surveillance revelations
timeline.src: Al Jazeera: Brazilian leader postpones US state visit

fu.t: Brazil selects Saab's Gripen over Boeing in the 36-jet F-X2 competition. USNI News says the US effort was 'derailed' by the spying revelation, though that is its own characterisation.
Rousseff visits the White House; the two governments issue a joint climate statement (record X-E1013).

timeline.ev: Enrique Peña Nieto's state visit to Beijing produces 14 agreements, including a planned fund of up to US$5bn for Pemex projects and a US$2.4bn joint investment fund. On 6 November, a week earlier, Mexico had revoked the 50.8bn-peso (about US$3.75bn) Mexico City–Querétaro high-speed rail award to a CRCC-led consortium.
timeline.sg: State visit; investment funds, market access
timeline.src: Expansión (ADN Político): Peña firma acuerdos en China entre polémica por concesión de tren revocada

fu.t: Finance minister Videgaray suspends the Mexico–Querétaro high-speed train indefinitely, citing budget cuts after the fall in oil prices.
Mexico agrees to compensate CRCC with almost Mex$20m (about US$1.3m) for the cancelled contract.

timeline.ev: Joe Biden speaks at the IDB conference where the presidents of Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador present the Plan of the Alliance for Prosperity. At a Blair House lunch, he says the US will seek significant increases in assistance and will set up an in-country refugee/parole programme for children.
timeline.sg: Migration root causes; Alliance for Prosperity
timeline.src: The White House (Obama archives): Readout of the Vice President's Central America Events Today
timeline.loc: Inter-American Development Bank and Blair House, Washington

fu.t: Congress provides up to US$750m for Central America to support the Northern Triangle strategy (existing record X-E223; the source is in that record).

timeline.ev: Rousseff returns to the White House. The two presidents issue a joint climate statement: Brazil will restore and reforest 12m hectares by 2030 and reach a 28–33% non-hydro renewables share in its energy mix, both aim for 20% non-hydro renewable electricity by 2030, and they create a Climate Change Working Group.
timeline.sg: Working visit after the 2013 surveillance rift; climate, trade
timeline.src: The American Presidency Project (UCSB), reproducing the White House text: Joint Statement by President Obama and President Dilma Rousseff of Brazil on Climate Change

timeline.ev: Lima hosts the APEC Leaders' Meeting (19–20 November 2016). Leaders commit to open markets and fight 'all forms of protectionism' and to keep studying a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. On the sidelines, Obama holds his last bilateral with Xi Jinping (19 November) and meets Pedro Pablo Kuczynski.
timeline.sg: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting
timeline.src: El Día (wire services, AP photo): Foro APEC reafirma en Perú defensa TLC

fu.t: Trump withdraws the US from the TPP (existing record X-E227). Nothing in the verified sources links this to APEC Lima.

timeline.ev: Mauricio Macri, on a state visit to China and at the first Belt and Road Forum, meets Xi Jinping. Argentina and China sign cooperation agreements worth about US$15bn, including a US$12.5bn agreement to build and finance two nuclear reactors (Atucha III and a fifth plant using Chinese technology), and agree to continue hydro, nuclear and rail projects.
timeline.sg: State visit and Belt and Road Forum
timeline.src: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Comercio Internacional y Culto (Argentina): President Macri in China and Japan

fu.t: Nucleoeléctrica and CNNC sign the EPC contract for Atucha III as a single 1,200 MWe Hualong One (existing record X-E626). This changes the 2017 two-reactor plan; the reasons were not verified here.
El Cronista reports that the Milei government decided to rule out Chinese companies from building nuclear power plants in Buenos Aires province.

timeline.ev: Six months after the Dominican Republic switched recognition (X-E051), Danilo Medina holds talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing. Xi proposes Belt and Road cooperation in infrastructure, finance, tourism and aviation, the leaders witness the signing of cooperation documents (18 by a later Dominican account), and a joint statement is issued.
timeline.sg: State visit after establishment of relations
timeline.src: Xinhua (Belt and Road Portal): China, Dominican Republic pledge to promote common development

fu.t: The executive promulgates the China–DR Air Services Agreement signed on 2 November 2018, after Congress approved it on 19 December 2022 (Resolución 373-22).
An Acento opinion column urges that the 18 agreements of 2018 be 'retomados', implying they were largely dormant.

timeline.ev: Amid mass protests, Sebastián Piñera cancels the APEC Leaders' Week planned for Santiago (11–17 November 2019) and COP25, removing the venue where Trump and Xi had been expected to sign a 'phase one' trade deal. The White House said signing plans were still in place.
timeline.sg: APEC 2019 host (cancelled)
timeline.src: NPR (via KUER): As Protests Persist, Chile's President Cancels 2 Major International Summits

timeline.ev: Nayib Bukele makes a state visit to Beijing and meets Xi Jinping. Xi offers help 'within its means' and invites El Salvador to build the Belt and Road. Cooperation documents and a joint statement are signed. CSIS reports MoUs for about US$500m in projects: a stadium, a US$40m national library, a La Libertad pier, US$85m for water treatment and US$200m for 'Surf City'.
timeline.sg: State visit after 2018 recognition
timeline.src: China Daily (Belt and Road Portal): President calls for enhanced ties with El Salvador

fu.t: CSIS (Ellis) reports the stadium still at site selection, no site for the library, cost overruns on water plants and the pier begun on 27 February 2021.
Bukele inaugurates the National Library (BINAES), built with US$54m of non-reimbursable Chinese cooperation.

timeline.ev: Federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, the president's son, blames China for Covid-19 and compares it with Chernobyl. Ambassador Yang Wanming demands an apology, and the embassy says he caught a 'mental virus' in Miami. House speaker Rodrigo Maia apologises, and Foreign Minister Ernesto Araújo calls the ambassador's response unacceptable and expects a retraction.
timeline.sg: Documented diplomatic tension
timeline.src: AFP (via Malay Mail): Bolsonaro son accuses China over Covid-19

fu.t: Anvisa approves emergency use of Sinovac's CoronaVac, produced with Butantan (existing record X-E353). This shows health cooperation continued despite the row.

timeline.ev: The US and Mexico relaunch the High-Level Economic Dialogue, dormant since 2016, with four pillars: Building Back Together; Sustainable Economic and Social Development in Southern Mexico and Central America; Securing the Tools for Future Prosperity; and Investing in Our People. Supply-chain coordination is included.
timeline.sg: Economic dialogue; supply chains
timeline.src: The American Presidency Project (UCSB), reproducing the White House text: Fact Sheet: U.S.-Mexico High-Level Economic Dialogue

timeline.ev: At the US–Mexico High-Level Security Dialogue in Mexico City, Blinken, Garland and Mayorkas meet López Obrador and Ebrard and outline the Bicentennial Framework for Security, Public Health and Safe Communities, replacing the 13-year Mérida Initiative's focus. A three-year plan was due by the end of January.
timeline.sg: Security dialogue
timeline.src: Associated Press (via ClickOrlando): Mexico and US working to build new security framework

fu.t: Rubio visits Mexico and a new bilateral security group is set up (existing record X-E272). That this is a successor to the Bicentennial Framework was not verified.

timeline.ev: Xi Jinping holds talks with Miguel Díaz-Canel in Beijing, among the first foreign leaders received after the 20th Party Congress. They sign documents on party exchanges, a foreign-ministry consultation mechanism, Belt and Road and practical cooperation, and a Joint Statement on Deepening China–Cuba Relations in the New Era. Xi pledges help with Cuba's difficulties and opposition to 'blockade'.
timeline.sg: State visit
timeline.src: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC (via GlobalSecurity.org): Xi Jinping Holds Talks with Cuban President (PRC MFA)
timeline.loc: Great Hall of the People, Beijing

fu.t: Xi approves an aid package for Cuba including US$80m and 60,000 t of rice (existing record X-E376). No source ties it to the 2022 visit.

timeline.ev: China's Defence Minister Wei Fenghe gives the keynote at the Fifth China–Latin American and Caribbean States Defense Forum ('Peace and Cooperation'), held by video link with defence and military leaders of 24 LAC countries.
timeline.sg: Security/defence dialogue
timeline.src: PLA Daily / China Military Online (via GlobalSecurity.org): PLA Daily report on the Fifth China-LAC Defense Forum

fu.t: The PRC Defence Ministry spokesperson describes the China–LAC States Defense Forum, a military medicine forum and senior-officer seminars as recurring mechanisms.

timeline.ev: Lula meets Biden at the White House. Their joint statement commits to defending democracy, revives the Climate Change Working Group and says the US will seek congressional funds for Amazon protection, including initial support for the Amazon Fund. Cooperation on 'social inclusion and labor rights' is pledged.
timeline.sg: Official visit; democracy, climate
timeline.src: The American Presidency Project (UCSB): Joint Statement by President Biden and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil

fu.t: Biden pledges to request US$500m over five years for the Amazon Fund and related activities, subject to Congress. This came days after Lula's visit to China (X-E085); analysts did not rule out a link, but there is no official statement.
Biden and Lula launch the Partnership for Workers' Rights in New York, the first joint US–Brazil global initiative on labour rights.

timeline.ev: Gustavo Petro meets Biden at the White House. The White House says the agenda covers climate, counter-narcotics, regional migration, economic and security cooperation, and human and labour rights, calling Colombia 'a key partner'. No commitments were announced in the pre-meeting statement.
timeline.sg: Bilateral meeting
timeline.src: The American Presidency Project (UCSB): Statement from White House Press Secretary Karine Jean-Pierre on the Bilateral Meeting between President Biden and President Petro

fu.t: Petro makes a state visit to Beijing and the two countries raise ties to a strategic partnership (existing record X-E363).
US Treasury sanctions Petro (existing record X-E117).

timeline.ev: Gabriel Boric meets Xi Jinping in Beijing during the third Belt and Road Forum and a state visit. Xi calls Chile a pioneer of Belt and Road cooperation in Latin America. Chile and China sign 13 cooperation agreements, including a Belt and Road cooperation plan and economic-development exchanges.
timeline.sg: State visit; Belt and Road Forum
timeline.src: Xinhua (Belt and Road Portal): (BRF2023) Xi holds talks with Chilean president

fu.t: BYD and Tsingshan drop planned Chilean lithium-value-added plants (existing record X-E655), citing prices and delays.
Boric meets Xi again in Beijing on the sidelines of the China–CELAC ministerial (record X-E1033).

timeline.ev: Antony Blinken meets Javier Milei and Foreign Minister Diana Mondino in Buenos Aires. He says Argentina 'can count' on US support to stabilise its economy, that the US is the largest foreign investor and that Washington wants US companies to stay the 'partner of choice'.
timeline.sg: Secretary of State visit
timeline.src: Buenos Aires Times: Blinken says Argentina can count on US support to stabilise economy

fu.t: Argentina announces it is joining the Minerals Security Partnership and signs a critical-minerals MOU with the US (existing records X-E255, X-E647).

timeline.ev: In Ushuaia, Milei meets SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Laura Richardson and announces an 'integrated naval base' with the United States, a logistics hub for the South Atlantic and Antarctica. El Cronista notes this effectively stalls a Chinese-planned multipurpose port near Río Grande.
timeline.sg: Security/defence cooperation; Antarctic logistics
timeline.src: El Cronista: Milei desde Ushuaia: 'Queremos reforzar nuestra alianza estratégica con EE.UU.'

timeline.ev: Dina Boluarte makes a state visit to Beijing; Xi Jinping urges on-schedule completion of Chancay and alignment of the BRI with Peru's needs. They sign a 2024–2029 Joint Action Plan and several cooperation documents, and announce that negotiations to upgrade the China–Peru FTA are complete.
timeline.sg: State visit ahead of APEC Lima 2024
timeline.src: Xinhua (english.gov.cn): Xi Jinping holds talks with Peruvian President Dina Boluarte
timeline.loc: Great Hall of the People, Beijing

fu.t: Xi and Boluarte inaugurate Chancay and witness the signing of the FTA upgrade protocol (existing records X-E094, X-E367).

timeline.ev: In San José, Marco Rubio praises Costa Rica for allowing only 'trusted vendors' in its 5G rollout, effectively excluding Chinese suppliers, and accuses Beijing of economic coercion. He announces aid waivers for security and counter-drug programmes and closer cybersecurity and biometric cooperation.
timeline.sg: Secretary of State Central America tour
timeline.src: US Department of State (via GlobalSecurity.org): Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Costa Rican President Rodrigo Chaves Robles at a Joint Press Availability

timeline.ev: After meeting Rubio in Guatemala City, Bernardo Arévalo agrees to accept third-country deportees from the US (returned home at US expense), to increase deportation flights by 40%, and to create a border security force for the Honduras and El Salvador borders.
timeline.sg: Migration and security
timeline.src: Associated Press (via WLRN): Guatemala agrees to accept migrants from other countries being deported from the US

timeline.ev: In Santo Domingo, Rubio and Luis Abinader discuss Haiti, energy and drugs. Rubio announces an MoU formalising a US CBP agent's work with the Dominican police, and Abinader highlights preliminary rare-earth reserves and a state company to explore them. China came up only in Rubio's remark on Chinese espionage in Cuba.
timeline.sg: Secretary of State Central America/Caribbean tour
timeline.src: American Rhetoric (transcript): Marco Rubio Joint Press Conference with Dominican Republic President Luis Abinader

fu.t: Hegseth signs an agreement in Santo Domingo giving US forces temporary access to parts of an air base (existing record X-E276).

timeline.ev: On the sidelines of the Fourth China–CELAC Ministerial, Boric holds his third meeting with Xi in four years. Boric says trade wars are not the way to handle differences. Xi offers to enrich and update the comprehensive strategic partnership, and they list trade, investment, Antarctic science and energy transition as priorities.
timeline.sg: Bilateral meeting at China–CELAC Forum (X-E107)
timeline.src: CNN Chile: Presidente Boric se reunió con Xi Jinping en Pekín

timeline.ev: After Colombia signed a Belt and Road cooperation plan in Beijing (X-E109), the US State Department's Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs said it would 'firmly oppose' IDB and other multilateral financing for Chinese state-owned enterprise projects in Colombia. Petro called the decision appropriate and argued that US firms should bid on Colombian projects.
timeline.sg: BRI accession and US response
timeline.src: Fundación Andrés Bello: Following the signing of the cooperation plan for the Belt and Road, the U.S. took measures against Colombia
pa: US Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs

fu.t: US Western Hemisphere Affairs announces opposition to multilateral financing of Chinese SOE projects in Colombia (the US measure itself; date not given in source).

timeline.ev: Trump hosts Milei at the White House twelve days before Argentina's midterms. Trump and Treasury Secretary Bessent tie the US$20bn swap to Milei's party doing well, and Trump says the US 'would not be generous with Argentina' if Milei lost.
timeline.sg: Bilateral meeting; financial support
timeline.src: Al Jazeera: 'Not going to waste our time': Trump hinges US aid to Argentina on election

fu.t: The Argentine central bank and US Treasury sign the US$20bn swap (existing record X-E116).
Milei's party wins the midterms (existing record X-E118).

timeline.ev: Trump and Claudia Sheinbaum meet in person for the first time, with Mark Carney, at the FIFA World Cup draw at the Kennedy Center. They talk ahead of the July 2026 USMCA joint review amid disputes over tariffs, cartels and US strikes; no agreement is reported.
timeline.sg: Informal leaders' meeting; USMCA, security
timeline.src: Associated Press (via KRGV): Trump meets Mexican President Sheinbaum in person for the first time at World Cup draw

fu.t: Mexico's Congress approves tariffs of up to 50% on Chinese and other non-FTA Asian imports (existing record X-E127). The measure had been proposed months earlier, so the meeting cannot be shown to have caused it.

timeline.ev: Yamandú Orsi meets Xi Jinping in Beijing on a seven-day state visit with a 150-person delegation, the first Latin American leader to visit China after the US capture of Maduro. They sign 12 cooperation agreements in science, technology and trade.
timeline.sg: State visit; trade and cooperation
timeline.src: Al Jazeera: Uruguay President Orsi deepens ties with China's Xi despite Trump threats
timeline.loc: Great Hall of the People, Beijing

timeline.ev: Lula meets Trump at the White House for about three hours, seeking to avert new tariffs under a Section 301 investigation and signalling willingness to cooperate on critical minerals (with domestic processing) and organised crime. Trump says it 'went very well' and that more meetings will follow; no agreement is announced.
timeline.sg: Trade (Section 301), critical minerals, organised crime
timeline.src: Reuters (via Daily Maverick): Brazil's Lula visits Trump in Washington seeking to avert new US trade tariffs

timeline.ev: China formally hands over Costa Rica's new National Stadium, a donation of about US$100m fully paid by the Chinese government and described as a cooperation commitment after Costa Rica broke with Taiwan in June 2007.
timeline.sg: Followup to 2007 diplomatic recognition
timeline.src: La Nación (Costa Rica): China hace entrega oficial del Estadio Nacional

fu.t: The stadium is delivered as a grant linked by the newspaper to the 2007 recognition switch.

timeline.ev: USTR imposed Section 301 'forced labor' tariffs on 60 economies from 24 July 2026, as the 150-day Section 122 surcharge expired: 10% on 17 economies including Argentina, Ecuador, Honduras and Mexico, and 12.5% on all other investigated economies except listed EU/Taiwan/Japan/Korea/Switzerland products. Chile, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela are among the 60; Bolivia, Panama and Paraguay are not. USMCA duty-free goods from Mexico are exempt.
timeline.sg: US Section 301 forced-labor tariffs
timeline.src: Office of the United States Trade Representative: USTR Takes Action in Forced Labor Section 301 Investigations

fu.t: BioBioChile: Chile at 12.5%, copper exempt

timeline.ev: US Ambassador Peter Lamelas told the AmCham Energy Forum that Chinese technology in strategic networks would deter investors in Vaca Muerta; the article also reports a Neuquén cooperative's Huawei purchase drew a US visa-restriction warning and that China's request to add equipment to its Neuquén deep-space station is under review.
timeline.sg: US diplomatic pressure on Chinese tech
timeline.src: Buenos Aires Herald (Matías Ortega): US issues strong warning to Argentina over China: 'It won't help attract investment'

timeline.ev: Argentina's central bank renewed its full swap line with the People's Bank of China (about US$19bn) for five years; the roughly US$5bn tranche activated since 2023 remains activated, with about US$680m reported outstanding. A Trump administration official had called the swap an 'extortionary arrangement'.
timeline.sg: PBoC swap renewal
timeline.src: Buenos Aires Times / Bloomberg (Manuela Tobias): Argentina renews US$19-billion China swap for another five years

timeline.ev: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met President Rodrigo Paz in New York during the UN General Assembly; per US official Juan Pablo Segura they discussed a possible new investment law to unlock US investment in AI, green energy, hydrocarbons and mining, and Rubio linked US ties to Bolivia's access to a US$1.9bn IMF credit.
timeline.sg: Rubio–Paz meeting at UNGA
timeline.src: Visión 360: EEUU ve clave una ley de inversiones en Bolivia para inyecciones de capital en hidrocarburos y minería

timeline.ev: The United States and Bolivia signed a Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals in Washington, with US State Department official Caleb Orr and Bolivian Mining Minister Marco Antonio Calderón de la Barca, committing to attract investment in lithium and other critical minerals to secure supply chains.
timeline.sg: US–Bolivia critical minerals MOU
timeline.src: Correo del Sur: Sellan pacto entre EEUU y Bolivia para explotar tierras raras

timeline.ev: Bolivia's hydrocarbons and energy minister Mauricio Paz Medinaceli said the Paz government would honour existing energy and lithium contracts signed by the previous government, including with Chinese and Russian companies, and seek a solution 'within the contract'.
timeline.sg: Bolivia lithium contracts review
timeline.src: Reuters (Lucinda Elliot, Monica Machicao), republished by Energy News: Bolivia promises to honour energy and lithium deals to reassure investors

timeline.ev: Brazil opened a formal process under its Economic Reciprocity Law (Lei 15.122/2025) against the 25% US Section 301 tariff in force since 22 July 2026: Camex circulated the request and Itamaraty notified Washington and requested consultations; no countermeasures were adopted.
timeline.sg: Brazil reciprocity process
timeline.src: Congresso em Foco: Brasil abre processo de reciprocidade contra tarifas dos EUA

timeline.ev: USTR imposed an additional 25% ad valorem tariff on all products of Brazil, with exemptions (e.g., certain civil aircraft, pharmaceuticals, goods under Section 232), effective 22 July 2026, after a Section 301 determination (1 June 2026) and a presidential memorandum (15 July 2026).
timeline.sg: US Section 301 tariff on Brazil
timeline.src: Office of the United States Trade Representative: Brazil Section 301 Final Action (Federal Register notice)

timeline.ev: At a Sofofa seminar marking 20 years of the Chile–China FTA, Chinese Ambassador Niu Qingbao urged Chile to resist 'external interference' that limits investment, criticised tariffs and coercive diplomacy without naming the US, and called relations with the Kast government 'very important, constructive and positive'.
timeline.sg: Chinese ambassador statement
timeline.src: La Tercera (Emiliano Carrizo): Embajador chino llama a Chile a protegerse de la 'injerencia externa' que limite las inversiones en el país

timeline.ev: President José Antonio Kast received Chinese Ambassador Niu Qingbao at La Moneda; they discussed the foreign minister's Asia trip and Kast's expected attendance at the APEC Leaders' Summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November 2026. The meeting came amid a dispute over the new US tariff, with US Ambassador Brandon Judd calling Chilean ministers' comments 'disappointing'.
timeline.sg: Kast–Niu meeting
timeline.src: BioBioChile: Presidente Kast se reúne con el embajador de China en Chile, Niu Qingbao, en La Moneda

timeline.ev: At his US Senate confirmation hearing, Trump's nominee for ambassador to Colombia, Nate Morris, said President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella had committed to ending Colombia's Belt and Road cooperation plan with China (signed May 2025).
timeline.sg: Colombia BRI exit signalled
timeline.src: EFE via SWI swissinfo.ch: De la Espriella se retirará de la iniciativa china de la Ruta de la Seda, dice EE.UU.

timeline.ev: The US State Department reported that Secretary Rubio spoke with President Laura Fernández to reaffirm the partnership, discussing security cooperation and the bilateral trade and investment relationship.
timeline.sg: Rubio–Fernández call
timeline.src: Panamá América (citing State Dept. spokesperson Tommy Pigott): Rubio dialoga con Laura Fernández sobre seguridad, comercio e inversión

timeline.ev: Wang Yi met Costa Rican Foreign Minister Manuel Tovar in New York; Tovar reaffirmed Costa Rica's 'firm commitment to the one-China policy' and readiness to raise relations to a 'new height' ahead of their 20th anniversary in 2027.
timeline.sg: Wang Yi–Tovar meeting
timeline.src: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC: Wang Yi Meets with Costa Rican Foreign Minister Manuel Tovar Rivera

timeline.ev: On a state visit to Beijing, President Daniel Noboa held talks with Xi Jinping, who cited the 'dividend' of the bilateral FTA and called for Belt and Road projects in energy, mining, infrastructure and finance; Noboa said Ecuador respects China's position on Taiwan. Cooperation documents on green industry, trade, digital economy and livelihoods were signed.
timeline.sg: Noboa state visit to China
timeline.src: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC: President Xi Jinping Holds Talks with Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa

timeline.ev: USTR Jamieson Greer and Ecuador's Minister of Production, Foreign Trade and Investment Luis Alberto Jaramillo signed the United States–Ecuador Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.
timeline.sg: US–Ecuador ART
timeline.src: Office of the United States Trade Representative: Ambassador Greer Signs the United States-Ecuador Agreement on Reciprocal Trade

timeline.ev: At the USMCA six-year joint review the United States did not confirm a 16-year extension, triggering annual joint reviews; Mexico and Canada supported extension. The agreement remains in force and US–Mexico bilateral negotiating rounds continued.
timeline.sg: USMCA joint review
timeline.src: White & Case LLP (citing USTR statement of 1 July 2026): USMCA 2026 Joint Review: United States declines to extend Agreement, triggering annual reviews

timeline.ev: The US Treasury (OFAC) sanctioned two sons of co-presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo and officials and entities in Nicaragua's gold sector, citing use of the industry to fund repression and the expropriation of a US-owned company.
timeline.sg: OFAC gold-sector sanctions
timeline.src: La Prensa (Nicaragua): Nicaragua's gold industry under fire: U.S. sanctions escalate pressure on Ortega

timeline.ev: CK Hutchison Holdings started investment-treaty arbitration against Panama, seeking more than US$1.5bn for the 'destruction' of its port investments after the annulment of the Panama Ports concession and the state takeover of Balboa and Cristóbal; a separate contract arbitration is being pursued by subsidiary Panama Ports Company.
timeline.sg: CK Hutchison treaty arbitration
timeline.src: Reuters (via KFGO): CK Hutchison seeks $1.5 billion from Panama in treaty dispute arbitration

timeline.ev: After talks with Secretary Rubio in Lima, President Keiko Fujimori announced Peru will join the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' security coalition against drug cartels; Al Jazeera notes China has overtaken the US as Peru's main trading partner and that Washington criticised the Chancay port in February.
timeline.sg: Peru joins Shield of the Americas
timeline.src: Al Jazeera (with Reuters, AP): Peru joins US-led 'Shield of the Americas' security alliance

timeline.ev: At the UN General Assembly President Santiago Peña said Paraguay 'is not neutral' on the Taiwan Strait and backed Taiwan's participation in the UN system.
timeline.sg: Peña UNGA speech
timeline.src: South China Morning Post: Paraguay's president urges UN to let Taiwan in, calls island's exclusion 'a stain'

timeline.ev: At the Mercosur summit in Luque, Paraguay's foreign minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano said Paraguay is open to trade with China as long as it does not have to sever ties with Taiwan.
timeline.sg: Paraguay China-trade statement
timeline.src: The China-Global South Project: Paraguay Says Open to Trade With China if Taiwan Ties Untouched

timeline.ev: Xi Jinping and Yamandú Orsi held talks in Beijing and witnessed the signing of over 10 cooperation documents (investment promotion, trade and others) and a joint statement on deepening the comprehensive strategic partnership; Orsi said Uruguay firmly supports the one-China principle.
timeline.sg: Orsi state visit to China
timeline.src: PRC Consulate/Embassy website (MFA readout): President Xi Jinping Holds Talks With Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi

timeline.ev: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez promised elections without a date at the UN General Assembly, a day after a brief meeting with President Trump on the sidelines in which they discussed restructuring Venezuela's sovereign debt.
timeline.sg: Rodríguez at UNGA; Trump meeting (22 Sep)
timeline.src: Al Jazeera (with AP, Reuters): Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez promises elections at UN, gives no date

timeline.ev: Venezuela's oil exports fell to about 1.08m b/d in September 2026 (from 1.17m in August); 629,000 b/d went to the US (553,000 in August), 253,000 b/d to India and about 86,000 b/d to Europe, per shipping data.
timeline.sg: Venezuelan oil export destinations
timeline.src: Reuters (Marianna Parraga, Mircely Guanipa) via EnergyNow: Venezuela's oil exports down in September amid high freight rates, data show

timeline.ev: Foreign Minister Mireya Agüero said Honduras is not in talks with Taiwan and that any decision between Taiwan and mainland China will be made on national-interest grounds through official channels.
timeline.sg: Honduras Taiwan/China stance
timeline.src: La Prensa (Honduras): ¿Honduras restablecerá relaciones diplomáticas con Taiwán? Canciller Agüero responde

timeline.ev: Honduras's Foreign Ministry stated it holds no talks or official contacts with Taiwanese authorities and will act according to existing diplomatic commitments; the Chinese embassy reaffirmed the one-China principle.
timeline.sg: Honduras denies Taiwan talks
timeline.src: Infobae: Honduras descarta conversaciones con Taiwán y reafirma relaciones diplomáticas con China

timeline.ev: China and El Salvador formally launched free trade agreement negotiations: China's Vice-Minister of Commerce Wang Shouwen and El Salvador's Minister of Economy María Luisa Hayem announced the launch by video link on Tuesday 16 April 2024.
timeline.sg: China–El Salvador FTA negotiations
timeline.src: China Daily Hong Kong (citing MOFCOM): China and El Salvador begin talks on free trade agreement

timeline.ev: El Salvador's Ministry of Economy said the first round of FTA negotiations with China ended in the week of 31 August 2024, covering intellectual property, services, customs, sanitary measures, technical regulations, e-commerce and SMEs.
timeline.sg: China–El Salvador FTA negotiations
timeline.src: Diario El Mundo (Yelter Herrera): El Salvador y China finalizan primera ronda de negociaciones para TLC

timeline.ev: China's ambassador Zhang Yanhui said China and El Salvador had held three in-depth rounds of FTA negotiations and had 'almost reached an agreement', hoping it could be signed and enter into force in 2026. No signature had been reported as of this record.
timeline.sg: China–El Salvador FTA negotiations
timeline.src: El Salvador in English: El Salvador and China Advance Toward Signing a Free Trade Agreement

timeline.ev: USTR Jamieson Greer and El Salvador's Minister of Economy María Luisa Hayem signed the US–El Salvador Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, which USTR called the first such agreement in the Western Hemisphere. The US removes reciprocal tariffs on goods listed in Annex I; El Salvador commits to non-tariff-barrier, IP, labor and digital-tax provisions and to restrict unauthorized re-export of EAR-controlled US items.
timeline.sg: US Agreements on Reciprocal Trade
timeline.src: Office of the United States Trade Representative: Ambassador Greer Signs the U.S.–El Salvador Agreement on Reciprocal Trade

timeline.ev: The new National Stadium built with Chinese cooperation reached 75% completion (Bukele on X). Its contract sets July 2027 for delivery; Ambassador Zhang Yanhui said it could be usable from February 2027 and finished in April–May 2027. Capacity: 50,000 seats, expandable to about 60,000.
timeline.sg: Bukele–Xi 2019 cooperation package
timeline.src: El Diario de Hoy (elsalvador.com): Estadio Nacional: avance de construcción

fu.t: INDES president Yamil Bukele: stadium could be finished late 2026 or early 2027; construction start delayed by Chinese contracting process.

timeline.ev: The White House said El Salvador's decision to recognise Beijing was of grave concern and 'will result in a reevaluation of our relationship with El Salvador', criticising the non-transparent decision and Chinese economic inducements.
timeline.sg: El Salvador recognition switch 2018
timeline.src: The White House (archived): Statement from the Press Secretary on El Salvador

timeline.ev: The State Department recalled Ambassador Jean Manes (El Salvador), Ambassador Robin Bernstein (Dominican Republic) and Chargé d'affaires Roxanne Cabral (Panama) for consultations over the three countries' decisions to stop recognising Taiwan.
timeline.sg: Recognition switches 2018
timeline.src: Revista E&N: EEUU llama a consultas a sus embajadores en El Salvador, Panamá y República Dominicana

timeline.ev: At an Oval Office meeting with Trump, Bukele refused to return wrongly deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia. The Trump administration pays El Salvador US$6m to hold deportees in the CECOT mega-prison; more than 200 migrants, many Venezuelans removed under the Alien Enemies Act, were sent there in March 2025.
timeline.sg: Bilateral meeting; deportation and security cooperation
timeline.src: NPR (via WFAE): El Salvador's Bukele says 'preposterous' to suggest he return Abrego Garcia to U.S.

timeline.ev: The US sanctioned six Cuban nationals and five entities over military procurement, including Cuba's military, naval and air attaché in Beijing, Waldo Pérez Cortés, said to be involved in procuring military-related equipment from China, and Tecnoimport, which imports military equipment from Russia and China.
timeline.sg: US maximum-pressure campaign on Cuba 2026
timeline.src: South China Morning Post: US sanctions Cuba's military representative in Beijing over China procurement

timeline.ev: China delivered a second donation of 5,000 photovoltaic systems (each with 14.3 kWh storage, reported as 3.6 kW) to Cuba for rural homes and essential services in all 169 municipalities, after 5,000 2-kW systems in November 2025, during the US fuel blockade.
timeline.sg: Chinese aid to Cuba 2026
timeline.src: pv magazine (Luis Ini): Cuba receives another 5,000 solar systems from China, expands renewable energy incentives

timeline.ev: The Dominican Republic and the US signed a critical minerals and rare earths cooperation framework (Foreign Minister Víctor-Ito Bisonó and US Ambassador Leah Campos) to identify projects, open financing channels and build a supply chain to separated material. It contains no dollar figure or enforceable obligations; Abinader cites over 150 Mt of rare-earth deposits in Pedernales.
timeline.sg: US critical-minerals frameworks
timeline.src: Latin Times (Mateo Moreno): Dominican Republic's rare earths deal with Washington: what's real, what's revised, what's still just a plan

timeline.ev: ProDominicana and the Dominican ambassador held a business forum in Beijing to attract Chinese investment in tourism, energy and technology (incl. AI and semiconductors). Dominican exports to China were US$325.8m in 2024 (+34.9%) and US$187.1m in Jan–Jul 2025. No agreements were reported.
timeline.src: Presidencia de la República Dominicana: República Dominicana presenta oportunidades de inversión en Foro de Negocios en Beijing

timeline.ev: Arévalo said Guatemala kept a security partnership with the US and used a pragmatic negotiating strategy on trade. The US–Guatemala Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, signed on 30 January 2026 by Minister Gabriela García and USTR Greer, lets 70.4% of Guatemalan exports enter the US at 0%, although Guatemala is not part of the US-backed 'Escudo de las Américas'.
timeline.sg: US Agreements on Reciprocal Trade
timeline.src: Agencia Guatemalteca de Noticias (AGN): Presidente Arévalo destaca relación económica con Estados Unidos

timeline.ev: On a visit to Taiwan, Arévalo signed with Taiwan's government a political-consultation mechanism, a letter of intent on investment through supply chains and a letter of intent on strategic semiconductor cooperation, which he called a new chapter in economic ties.
timeline.src: Agencia Guatemalteca de Noticias (AGN): Presidente Arévalo fortalece relaciones y alcanza acuerdos con República de China (Taiwán) y Japón

timeline.ev: The UN Security Council adopted resolution 2793 (2025), drafted by Panama and the US, to replace the Kenya-led mission with a Gang Suppression Force of up to 5,500 uniformed personnel, by 12–0 with China, Russia and Pakistan abstaining. China's representative criticised a country that had 'conveniently forgotten its commitments' on funding.
timeline.src: United Nations: Security Council 10009th Meeting (PM), SC/16185

timeline.ev: Haiti's new UN-backed Gang Suppression Force had more than US$200m pledged by 13 Security Council members (US$59m disbursed). Chadian troops were already in Port-au-Prince and all 5,500 personnel were expected by the end of 2026.
timeline.src: AP (via NY1): Haiti's new UN-backed gang-fighting force exceeds funding expectations

timeline.ev: Officials of Haiti and Taiwan met in Taipei to mark 70 years of formal diplomatic ties. Taiwan's MOFA still lists Haiti as an ally on its page last updated 1 October 2026; Haiti has no relations with the PRC.
timeline.src: TaiwanPlus: Taiwan and Haiti celebrate 70 years of diplomatic ties

timeline.ev: Mexico's Secretaría de Economía publishes a decree in the Diario Oficial temporarily raising import duties to between 5% and 50% on 544 tariff lines (steel, aluminium, textiles, apparel, footwear, wood, plastics, chemicals, electrical materials and others) from countries without a trade agreement, effective 23 April 2024 for two years.
timeline.sg: Raise tariffs on imports from non-FTA partners (not named in the source; China is the main affected supplier in context).
timeline.src: Holland & Knight: Import duties of 544 HTS codes are temporarily modified in Mexico

fu.t: Superseded by the permanent LIGIE reform covering about 1,463 lines (X-E906).

timeline.ev: The US and Mexico jointly announce steel and aluminium measures: Proclamation 10783 imposes a 'melt and pour' requirement so that Mexican steel melted and poured outside Mexico, Canada or the US pays Section 232 duties, and Mexican aluminium containing metal smelted or cast in China, Russia, Belarus or Iran faces higher duties. Mexico commits to require melt-and-pour reporting and to raise tariffs on non-FTA steel and aluminium.
timeline.sg: Prevent Chinese and other non-North American steel and aluminium from entering the US via Mexico under the 2019 232 exemption.
timeline.src: Thompson Hine (SmarTrade blog): United States and Mexico Act to Protect North American Steel and Aluminum Markets from Unfair Trade

fu.t: Proclamation 10896 terminates the Mexico steel arrangement, applying full Section 232 tariffs to Mexican steel (X-E905).

timeline.ev: US Customs and Border Protection determines under the Enforce and Protect Act (EAPA case 7801) that Minth Mexico Coatings, S.A. de C.V., Mexican subsidiary of the Chinese auto-parts group Minth, evaded antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chinese aluminium extrusions. The allegation was that Chinese-origin auto parts were repackaged in Mexico and declared as Mexican origin.
timeline.sg: Enforcement of AD/CVD orders on aluminium extrusions from China.
timeline.src: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Trade Remedy Law Enforcement Directorate: EAPA Case 7801: Notice of Determination as to Evasion (TRLED)

timeline.ev: President Claudia Sheinbaum presents Plan México. Its goals include producing 50% of supply and consumption in strategic sectors domestically, raising national content in global value chains (autos, electronics, semiconductors and others) by 15%, and offering incentives such as immediate deduction of new investment under a relocation decree valid to 2030. The plan is framed as a response to Asian competition through greater North American integration.
timeline.sg: Import substitution (mainly of Asian/Chinese goods) and greater regional integration with the US and Canada.
timeline.src: Expansión: 12 metas del Plan México (title per URL slug)

fu.t: LIGIE tariff reform publishes higher tariffs on non-FTA imports with stated aims of raising national content (X-E906).

timeline.ev: Proclamation 10896 terminates the 2019 Section 232 steel arrangement with Mexico (and Canada) as of 12 March 2025, making Mexican steel subject to full Section 232 tariffs. It cites rising import volumes and Mexico's imports from China as evidence of transshipment.
timeline.sg: Address alleged transshipment and import surges.
timeline.src: Executive Office of the President (United States): Proclamation 10896 of February 10, 2025: Adjusting Imports of Steel Into the United States

timeline.ev: Mexico publishes in the Diario Oficial (29 December 2025) the reform raising import duties on about 1,463 tariff lines (chapters 39, 50-63, 72, 73 and 87; rates 5-50%, mostly 35%) for non-FTA countries, effective 1 January 2026. The stated aims are to reduce dependence on foreign inputs, protect domestic producers, raise national content of exports, integrate supply chains and correct trade imbalances.
timeline.sg: Stated: 'reducir la dependencia de México respecto de insumos de origen extranjero' and raise national content.
timeline.src: Galicia Abogados: Actualización: Comercio. Reforma 2026 TIGIE

timeline.ev: A second tariff decree (DOF, 23 April 2026, evening edition) modifies import duties on 185 tariff lines (5-35%) and amends the PROSEC sectoral promotion decree, setting specified flat-rolled and alloy steel lines to duty-free for the electrical, electronics and automotive programmes. It takes effect 24 April 2026.
timeline.sg: Fine-tune the 2026 tariff structure; secure duty-free access to certain steel inputs for PROSEC manufacturers.
timeline.src: IDC Online: Segunda reforma arancelaria: el impacto de la reducción en PROSEC

timeline.ev: At the USMCA six-year joint review on 1 July 2026, the United States declines to confirm a 16-year extension. Mexico and Canada support renewal. The agreement stays in force to 2036, subject to annual joint reviews under Article 34.7.
timeline.sg: Leverage over the agreement's 'shortcomings' and trade deficits.
timeline.src: Office of the United States Trade Representative: Ambassador Greer Issues Statement on USMCA Joint Review

fu.t: Fourth round of US-Mexico bilateral negotiations scheduled (economic security, steel/aluminium, auto rules of origin).

timeline.ev: A 10% Section 301 tariff on imports from Mexico takes effect after USTR finds that Mexico does not effectively enforce its ban on imports made with forced labour. USMCA-compliant goods and products under Section 232 are exempt.
timeline.sg: Section 301 action on forced-labour import bans (part of investigations of about 60 economies launched in Feb 2026 after the Supreme Court invalidated IEEPA tariffs).
timeline.src: Congressional Research Service: U.S.-Mexico Trade Relations (IF11175)

timeline.ev: The White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy publishes 'The Great Transshipment Scam', listing more than 40 economies as risk routes for China-linked goods and placing Mexico in Tier 1 ('Diversified Scale Leaders'). It cites existing EAPA authority and a CBP AI tool in development ('Detective Border'). It gives no Mexico-specific estimate.
timeline.sg: Justify tighter origin enforcement; uses broad 'China-linked goods' concept (Chinese ownership/financing, supplier relationships, China-based production steps).
timeline.src: Arnold & Porter: White House Transshipment Report Signals Increased Scrutiny
pa: White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy

timeline.ev: Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard proposes to auto suppliers, at a private meeting in Detroit, a task force with major companies operating in Mexico to reduce imports from China ahead of Trump's inauguration.
timeline.sg: Substitute Chinese inputs in North American auto supply chains.
timeline.src: Bloomberg: Mexico Pitches Auto Suppliers Task Force to Curb China Imports

timeline.ev: At Canacero's 78th General Assembly, incoming president Sergio de la Maza Jiménez blames Chinese overproduction and subsidised dumping for the crisis in Mexican steel. He also criticises US Section 232 tariffs and calls for a regional North American steel policy, with Economy Secretary Ebrard present and pledging to defend domestic steel.
timeline.sg: Industry lobbying for protection against Chinese steel and for a regional steel arrangement with the US.
timeline.src: La Razón: Aranceles y dumping chino asestan golpe a la industria acerera

timeline.ev: After Secretary Rubio told President Mulino on 2 Feb 2025 that Chinese presence in the canal area was 'unacceptable' and that, absent immediate changes, the US would act under the 1977/1999 treaty, Panama announced it would not renew (and could terminate early) its BRI memorandum and reviewed the Hutchison port concession. Panama's Supreme Court annulled the concession on 29 Jan 2026; from 23–24 Feb 2026 APM Terminals (Maersk) took over Balboa and TiL (MSC) Cristóbal under 18-month interim contracts. Hutchison's US$22.8bn sale to BlackRock–TiL remained stalled in Aug 2026, and Hutchison/PPC are pursuing arbitration.
timeline.src: AP / PBS NewsHour: Rubio presses Panama to reduce Chinese influence over its canal or face U.S. measures

fu.t: Reuters (via gCaptain): Mulino says Panama's BRI agreement will not be renewed and could be terminated early; Rubio credits '@POTUS leadership'.
APM Terminals begins temporary operation of Balboa and TiL Panama of Cristóbal, each under an 18-month contract, after the annulment of CKHH's concessions.
CK Hutchison says there is 'absolutely nothing to report' on the BlackRock–MSC transaction; PPC seeks damages via arbitration; sources say COSCO is the unnamed additional strategic investor sought.

timeline.ev: After Pompeo's October 2018 warning in Panama about Chinese 'predatory' economic activity, the Cortizo government (from July 2019) cooled ties: it dropped the US$4.1bn Chinese-funded Panama–Chiriquí high-speed rail project in September 2019, and the Panama Maritime Authority cancelled the Landbridge-linked Panama Colón Container Port concession in June 2021 for non-payment and delays. US pressure also reportedly ended China's plan for a large embassy at the canal entrance.
timeline.src: Americas Quarterly (E. Sweigart, G. Cohen): Panama's Evolving Relationship with China

fu.t: Executive Decree 90 orders expropriation of 41 PCCP properties on Margarita Island (Colón); the AMP had cancelled the concession in June 2021 and again in April 2025. No US pressure mentioned.

timeline.ev: In April 2019 Pompeo warned in Santiago that Huawei was controlled by the Chinese government and that using it posed risks to Chile's citizens. In July 2020 Chile chose the Japanese-proposed route to Australia and New Zealand over the Huawei-backed route ending in Shanghai. The officially stated reason was that all financial indicators favoured that route. Neither trans-Pacific cable was built until the Google–Desarrollo País Humboldt cable (Valparaíso–Sydney) was signed in June 2025; it is approved, with laying planned for late 2026 and commercial operation for 2027.
timeline.src: El Mostrador (citing Nikkei): En Japón destacan el desaire de Chile a China en la elección de la ruta para el cable transoceánico

fu.t: Chile and Google sign the Humboldt cable agreement (14,800 km, Valparaíso–Sydney via French Polynesia; US$300–550m estimated; Chile contributes about US$25m; deployment envisaged for 2027).
Coastal-use commission approves Humboldt; Subtel says laying begins late 2026 and commercial operation is projected for 2027.

timeline.ev: In January 2026 Chile's telecom ministry approved, and two days later rescinded, a request linked to China Mobile for a Valparaíso–Hong Kong cable. On 20–21 Feb 2026 the State Department made Transport Minister Juan Carlos Muñoz and two other officials ineligible for US entry, saying they had compromised critical telecommunications infrastructure. Boric said he ordered the retraction after US threats. Under Kast the project is 'in the freezer' with no final decision, and Humboldt has priority.
timeline.src: gCaptain (Bloomberg): U.S. revokes visas for Chilean officials over China undersea cable

fu.t: Rest of World: Boric said he ordered the retraction after US threats of long-term consequences; after 11 March the US ambassador said the project was 'over'; Kast officials say it 'continues to be assessed'.
Ex-Ante: the file sits with the Defence and Foreign ministries; Kast: 'Primero vamos a concretar el cable Humboldt. Después conversamos'.

timeline.ev: Brazil endorsed the principles of the US Clean Network on 10 Nov 2020 during Keith Krach's visit, when the US offered financing to Brazilian operators to buy from Western vendors. Yet the 29 Jan 2021 ministerial ordinance allowed Huawei to participate subject to conditions, requiring only a separate private high-security network for federal government communications. After the November 2021 auction, TIM Brasil named Ericsson and Huawei as its 5G equipment suppliers.
timeline.src: Poder360: Portaria permite Huawei no leilão do 5G, mas governo exige rede exclusiva

fu.t: TIM Brasil names Ericsson and Huawei as 5G equipment suppliers.

timeline.ev: Under US pressure from Ambassador Marc Stanley and SOUTHCOM's Gen. Richardson, the Milei government sent an inspection delegation to the Chinese deep-space station in Neuquén (April 2024), but the station kept operating. In 2026 China's request to add equipment was referred to the Defence Ministry, where the Air Force recommended inventories, inspections and no new antenna. In August 2026 Ambassador Lamelas warned that Chinese technology would deter Vaca Muerta investors, and the Neuquén cooperative CALF made public a communication on US visa restrictions for executives expanding Huawei's operations.
timeline.src: Buenos Aires Herald: US issues strong warning to Argentina over China: 'It won't help attract investment'

fu.t: Government delegation (Cosentino, Antelo, ENACOM, CONAE) inspects the station after 'heavy pressure from Washington'; no findings published.
Government evaluates halting the China–Argentina radio telescope (CART) in San Juan and prepares an action plan on the Neuquén base; an official says 'la decisión es reducir la presencia china'.

timeline.ev: Trump's envoy Mauricio Claver-Carone called Argentina's PBoC swap 'extortion' (April 2025), and Treasury Secretary Bessent said Milei was committed to 'getting China out of Argentina' (October 2025), while stating that US aid was not conditioned on ending the swap. Argentina nevertheless renewed the activated US$5bn tranche in April 2025 and, on 5 Aug 2026, the full ~US$19bn line. About US$680m of the activated tranche was outstanding.
timeline.src: Buenos Aires Times: Argentina renews US$19 billion China swap for another five years

fu.t: Argentina extends the US$5bn activated tranche for a year after Claver-Carone called the swap 'extortion'.

timeline.ev: Argentina's Atucha III EPC contract with CNNC for a Hualong One reactor (Feb 2022) was annulled at a Nucleoeléctrica Argentina shareholders' meeting on 23 Sep 2026, citing lack of funds under the emergency law. The meeting authorised a tender for a privately financed reactor on the site, where the US-incorporated Meitner Energy (60% Ansari Group, 40% an INVAP-controlled US firm) plans a US$1.2bn ACR-300 SMR. US diplomacy had opposed Chinese technology at Atucha since at least 2022–23.
timeline.src: Diario Jornada (from Página/12): Alineado con EE.UU., el gobierno canceló Atucha III

fu.t: Economy Minister Caputo announces Meitner Energy's US$1.2bn private ACR-300 (300 MWe) SMR at the Atucha complex, pending ARN licensing.

timeline.ev: Ecuador joined the US Clean Network in November 2020. In January 2021 the DFC signed a framework to help refinance up to US$3.5bn of Ecuador's debt to China, reportedly with a commitment to keep Chinese firms out of its telecom networks. No disbursement was found. In September 2022 Ecuador instead restructured about US$3.2bn of loans with CDB and China Exim (≈US$1.4bn relief to 2025). The CEIEC-built ECU-911 surveillance platform kept operating, though the 2020 US Treasury sanction on CEIEC complicated its modernisation.
timeline.src: Center for Global Development (Landers, Lee, Morris): Why Does DFC Want to Pay Ecuador's Chinese Creditors?

fu.t: State Department briefing: Ecuador becomes the 51st Clean Network member.
Ecuador restructures CDB (US$1.4bn) and China Exim (US$1.8bn) loans, extending maturities to 2027 and 2032.
Vistazo: ECU-911 still depends on the CEIEC platform; officials say the OFAC sanction and the closed protocol complicate work with CEIEC; no replacement contracted.

timeline.ev: On 7 Sep 2018 the State Department recalled its chiefs of mission in the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Panama for consultations over their switches from Taipei to Beijing. The White House had said El Salvador's switch would 'result in a re-evaluation' of relations. None of the three switches was reversed. In El Salvador, China's proposed La Unión port/SEZ package stalled, and the US promoted a DFC-backed LNG power plant at Acajutla, which reached commercial operation in October 2022.
timeline.src: CNA (Focus Taiwan) via GlobalSecurity: U.S. calls back ambassadors over severing of ties with Taiwan

fu.t: CSIS (Ellis): the La Unión logistics hub and six-SEZ proposal was blocked by political, legal and other obstacles; the US offered the DFC-backed Acajutla LNG plant and América Crece.
Invenergy confirms commercial operations at the 378 MW Energía del Pacífico LNG-to-power plant (US$1bn project).

timeline.ev: SOUTHCOM's Gen. Richardson raised dual-use and data-security concerns about Chancay (May 2024), and Trump transition adviser Claver-Carone proposed a 60% tariff on 'any product going through Chancay' (16 Nov 2024). The port opened on 14 Nov 2024 and kept growing: 200,000 TEU in H1 2026, up 70.9% year on year.
timeline.src: Bloomberg via gCaptain: Trump ally urges duties on goods shipped via China's Peru port

fu.t: Chancay handles 200,000 TEU in H1 2026 (+70.94% y/y) and 987,000 t of bulk/general cargo (+41.2%).

timeline.ev: US measures (the IRA's foreign-entity-of-concern rules from 1 Dec 2023, which bar FEOC battery components from 2024 and FEOC-processed critical minerals from 2025 for the clean-vehicle credit; tariff threats and Section 232 auto tariffs in 2025) reduced the US-market rationale for Chinese EV and battery plants in Mexico. BYD's Mexican plant was not built: China's Ministry of Commerce withheld approval over fears of technology leaking to the US (FT, March 2025), and BYD put it on hold in July 2025. CATL postponed announcing a Mexico/US plant in August 2022 amid US–China tension and did not build in Mexico.
timeline.src: Mexico News Daily (citing Financial Times): FT: China is withholding approval for BYD's Mexico plant due to tech concerns

fu.t: Bloomberg: CATL pushes back announcing a North American plant (Mexico sites near Texas, and US sites) for Tesla and Ford, amid the Pelosi visit.

timeline.ev: After Colombia signed a BRI cooperation plan (14 May 2025), the State Department's Western Hemisphere bureau said it would 'firmly oppose' IDB and other multilateral financing for projects by Chinese state firms, which put at risk the Chinese-built Bogotá Metro Line 1. Bogotá said its financing was secured, and Line 1 passed 70% progress by January 2026 with completion targeted for March 2028.
timeline.src: Bloomberg Línea: Petro ignora la decisión de EE.UU. de desfinanciar proyectos chinos en Colombia

fu.t: Bogotá mayoralty says the works have 'todo el soporte financiero' and will finish Line 1 by March 2028.
Provisional: the US ambassador nominee says President-elect de la Espriella committed to ending Colombia's BRI participation (X-E715).

timeline.ev: Bolivia's lithium contracts with CATL-led CBC (≈US$1.03bn) and Russia's Uranium One, signed under Arce and sent to the legislature, were suspended by a Potosí court in 2025, put under review by the Paz government (Nov 2025), and, as of February 2026, had not been approved. Meanwhile the US and Bolivia signed a critical-minerals MOU on 27 Apr 2026. No specific US measure against the contracts was found.
timeline.src: Correo del Sur: Sellan pacto entre EEUU y Bolivia para explotar tierras raras

fu.t: Paz's economic chief Lupo: all lithium contracts to be reviewed; 'If there's something positive to resume, it will be resumed.'

timeline.ev: China Southern Power Grid International's US$2.92bn purchase of 83.15% of Enel Distribución Perú (now Pluz, about 1.6m customers in Lima and Callao), financed by a US$2.3bn China Exim loan, was approved by INDECOPI in June 2024 and completed. No US government objection specific to the deal was found; the warnings came from Peru's industry association SNI and from a US congressional commission's general report.
timeline.src: IEA, China's official energy finance in emerging and developing economies: Case 2: Southern Power Grid's acquisition of Enel Peru distribution assets

timeline.ev: On 17–18 Sep 2020 Pompeo urged Guyana and Suriname to prefer US private firms, saying 'No state-owned operation can beat' them. Guyana nonetheless signed a US$260m contract (May 2022) with a China Railway Construction joint venture for the New Demerara River Bridge, took a €160.8m Bank of China loan (Dec 2022), and opened the bridge on 5–6 Oct 2025, while remaining a close US security partner.
timeline.src: Guyana Chronicle (state-owned): New Bharrat Jagdeo Demerara River Bridge opens to commuters from today
